PR.t: You don't have to wait for the letter. Paying the calculated amount now stops the growth on whatever you paid.
Keep the envelope - and the postmark. They are proof of when something was filed or paid.
If the mistake was the preparer's, put it in writing. Liability is investigated and assigned, not assumed.
A notice shows a total. Always ask for the work behind the total - every figure can be checked.
Puerto Rico runs its own code: late filing steps up 5%, then 10% per additional 30 days, capped at 25%.
Puerto Rico interest is a flat 10% per year - it does not compound daily the way federal interest does.

GU.t: This territory mirrors the federal code: the same penalties and rates apply, collected by the local taxing authority.
First-time penalty abatement exists: with three clean years - everything filed, and paid or on a payment plan - a first late penalty can be waived. You have to ask.
Interest never sleeps, but penalties often stop once a payment plan is accepted. The plan's real cost is the interest that keeps running.
Filing late costs 5% a month; paying late costs 0.5%. Filing on time - even without the money - is ten times cheaper.
An extension of time to file is not an extension of time to pay. Interest runs from the original due date either way.

CNMI.t: This territory mirrors the federal code: the same penalties and rates apply, collected by the local taxing authority.
First-time penalty abatement exists: with three clean years - everything filed, and paid or on a payment plan - a first late penalty can be waived. You have to ask.
Interest never sleeps, but penalties often stop once a payment plan is accepted. The plan's real cost is the interest that keeps running.
Filing late costs 5% a month; paying late costs 0.5%. Filing on time - even without the money - is ten times cheaper.
An extension of time to file is not an extension of time to pay. Interest runs from the original due date either way.
